title: Add clocksource ring-buffer sampling + tiled-kernel microbench and perf export
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need low-overhead, high-fidelity timing for short-lived tiled kernels and the kernel-selection path to guide scheduling and quantized-kernel choices. NVTX ranges and CUPTI integrations are great for coarse visibility, but they either require heavy vendor dependencies or introduce jitter at sub-microsecond scales. This change introduces a lightweight ring-buffer clocksource sampler (clocksource ringbuf) and a tiled-kernel microbenchmark harness that can exercise kernel selection heuristics across sequence-length/batch-size axes and export compact heatmaps for dashboards.

What this PR does: Adds a clocksource-based ring buffer that samples timestamps at entry/exit points in the runtime hot path; the buffer is very small (configurable, default 4096 entries) and lock-free on the fast path. Adds per-kernel cycle counters integrated into the kernel dispatch shim. Adds a tiled-kernel microbench harness under tools/perf/tiled_microbench that runs combinations of tile sizes, seq-lens, and batches, producing CSV heatmaps and a gzipped artifact for uploads. Adds a small export utility to convert ring-buffer traces into a compact GPU-agnostic CSV suitable for Grafana heatmap panels.

Design notes: The ring buffer uses a single-writer multi-reader layout; the writer is the runtime dispatch thread which writes a 64-bit monotonic timestamp and a 32-bit tag (encoded event id + flags). Readers (post-processing tools) handle wrap correctly. The microbench harness runs kernels in controlled loops with warmup and optional KV cache toggles to see the delta when cache hits occur. All new code paths are guarded behind a runtime flag (--perf-sample=ringbuf or env REDWOOD_PERF_RINGBUF) to avoid any default overhead.

Testing & CI: Unit tests validate ring-buffer wrap correctness and tag decoding. The microbench has a smoke runner that runs on CI GPUs with tiny sizes and is gated behind a perf/optional job to avoid slowing PR jobs. I added a CI artifact step to attach the CSV/gz artifact on success for manual inspection.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of ring-buffer clocksource sampler
- [x] Per-kernel cycle counters in dispatch shim
- [x] Tiled kernel microbench harness with CSV export
- [x] Grafana-compatible heatmap exporter script
- [x] Unit tests for sampling correctness
- [x] Lightweight CI perf smoke job (optional)

Related: This work is complementary to previous instrumentation (NVTX and CUPTI) but intentionally avoids external vendor dependencies for quick production profiling during incident response. See ENG-1827 and pr-25678 for cross-reference.

Notes for reviewers: The patch touches hot-path code (dispatch shim). I kept the fast-path writes to be a single relaxed atomic and a store to a per-thread buffer; please focus reviews on the memory ordering in dispatch_shim.cc and the conditional compilation macros. The perf export script is intentionally minimal and uses only Python stdlib and numpy if available.

Release notes: Adds optional low-overhead runtime sampling and a microbenchmark harness for tiled kernels; users can opt-in via runtime flag and upload CSV artifacts to the perf dashboard.

review_comments: Diego Mendez: Left a couple of questions about the atomic ordering on the ring buffer writer — why relaxed versus release?
Asha Patel (author): Relaxed is sufficient for the single-writer model; added explanatory comment and a small assert in debug builds to validate visibility. See updated dispatch_shim.cc
Riley Chen: Suggested reducing default ring size to 4096 from 16384 for lower memory on small nodes; made configurable and lowered default.
Priya Nair: Asked for a clearer CSV format with header metadata; export script updated to include runtime flags and git sha.
QA: Verified microbench artifacts for two GPU shapes in internal perf lab; artifacts uploaded and attached to the PR CI run.
release_notes: Adds opt-in low-overhead clocksource ring-buffer sampling and a tiled-kernel microbenchmark harness. Use --perf-sample or REDWOOD_PERF_RINGBUF to enable. Includes CSV/GZIP artifacts for dashboard import.
